text:
Esa Lindell has one point in 17 games, and the Stars couldn't care less. He's playing 23:23 a night and over 25 lately, with Dallas leaning on its defense through injuries, and the team has won eight of his last ten.

That's what he's for. Evolving-Hockey had him ninth among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement last season, nearly all of it from taking chances away: opponents got fewer expected goals with him on than with almost any other defenseman in the league. This season the Stars are about even in chances with him on at five on five, and he's blocked 39 shots.

The offense is what it is. No goals on 0.6 expected, and his shot grades out near the bottom of the league by NHL Edge. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flags one weak spot: only 30% of his exits keep possession.

Jesse Granger of The Athletic had the line of the week from Vegas: Lindell tried to hit Tomas Hertl, and it looked like he ran into a metal pole. What to watch: the minutes. He's taking on a lot.
